text:
hana: quick flag  onboarding keystone-6b-lite (hf -> redwood int4). fp16 baseline looks good but int4 exhibits prompt-dependent token aliasing on multi-sentence inputs.
pablo: aliasing how? example?
hana: prompt:
"Summarize:
Paragraph1...
Paragraph2..."
FP16 top tokens at boundary: ['\n','Paragraph2','\n']
INT4: ['Paragraph2','\n','Paragraph1']
ivy: that smells like a rotation/sign mismatch in rotary+proj when head groups are concatenated differently. did the exporter include any head_layout metadata?
hana: it has a weird field `attn_pack=chunked` in checkpoint.json. converter ignored it. I tried re-run forcing `--proj_order=interleaved` and `--head_pack=chunked` but no luck.
kevin: also check tokenizer normalizers. keystone's vocab has a multibyte combining mark that HF fast sometimes decomposes; that can change token boundary alignment at sentence breaks, shifting subsequent KV indices.
pablo: quick probe: run per-head logit diffs and compare cosine similarity per head between fp16 and int4 outputs. small script: 
```
python tools/compare_heads.py --fp16 ckpt_fp16.bin --quant converted_int4.bin --prompt-file tests/multi_para.txt --dump=cos
```
ivy: ran this locally: heads [2,3,7] show low cos (<0.2) and head offsets appear cyclic by 2 in the failing layer. when I permute those heads and recompute, cos goes >0.9.
hana: interesting. can we autodetect by scanning small sample set across perm candidates and pick the permutation with highest avg cos?\e ci-bot: issue RED-977 created: "keystone-6b-lite int4 head-perm + tokenizer normalization" (severity: medium)
kevin: yes, algo idea: for each candidate mapping within small group size (2..4), compute per-head correlation to fp16 on a micro-bench and pick best. fallback to user-specified mapping if ambiguity > threshold.
pablo: also add per-head scale calibration AFTER permuting, asymmetric quant helps many of these.
ivy: I'll prototype a lightweight autodetect in convert that tries group sizes 2,4 and both proj_orders and emits metadata: "head_perm", "proj_order", "tokenizer_normalizer". add a small smoke test that runs 10 short prompts and asserts token-level edit distance < 2 vs fp16.
hana: can you include a tokenizer_hash in metadata so Console can warn if client tokenizer differs?
ivy: yup. planning to open PR with tests + small bench today. target merge: EOD.
kevin: one caveat: permuting heads changes KV-cache layout; ensure we update cache index mapping and include note in rollout docs.
hana: thanks all. dropping short logs + failing prompt set in RED-977. will ping when PR is up.
